assessment: The token engine is the best-assembling thing in the deck and needs no help: eight multipliers at 78.2%, nine lords at 83.2%. What binds is the answer suite. Reading all 97 maindeck cards, exactly one — Anguished Unmaking — removes an opposing artifact or enchantment of mana value 3 or less, and that is the mana value of Torpor Orb, Ghostly Prison, Propaganda and Ensnaring Bridge; Despark is gated to 4 or greater and nothing touches a land. So the top six are answers and converters, ranked so that the ones which also make a body or a token come first. Divine Visitation and Coat of Arms are the famous token cards that miss the cut: this deck kills by trigger, not by combat, and neither adds a trigger.

ten.why: {2}{W} instant, destroy target permanent — the only card in the identity that reaches all four blanks (Torpor Orb at 2, Ghostly Prison, Propaganda and Ensnaring Bridge at 3) and also the land class, which no card in the 97 answers.
ten.unlocks: Instant-speed removal of the artifact that turns off the four-card conversion layer, held up on the same three mana the deck already keeps open for Boros Charm.

ten.why: Exiles a nonland, nontoken permanent you don't control at mana value 4 or less — every one of the four cards that blanks a kill route — and it is a creature, so it also triggers Impact Tremors, Purphoros and Warleader's Call on the way in.
ten.unlocks: An answer that pays the conversion layer instead of costing it a turn; exile also beats indestructible and regeneration, which Anguished Unmaking's exile is currently the only other source of.

ten.closes: engine: THE DRAIN DOUBLER — the drain-source half beside Bloodletter of Aclazotz
ten.why: "Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life" is the only card in the identity that converts the eminence token itself into life loss at all three seats, and it is a third drain source for Bloodletter beside Sanctum Seeker and Throne of the God-Pharaoh — a component measured at 5.3% drawn, 2.9% by turn six.
ten.unlocks: A conversion trigger that fires off token creation rather than a creature entering, so it survives Torpor Orb, which blanks all four of the current converters at once.

ten.why: {1}{W}{B}, destroy target permanent, no mana value gate and no nonland clause — the second card that can point at an opposing land, the one permanent class the 97 leaves entirely uncovered.
ten.unlocks: A turn-three answer to Ghostly Prison or a Maze of Ith on the turn the swarm wants to attack, on a white-black cost the deck's 21 white and 26 black sources both clear.

ten.closes: engine: An answer to a noncreature permanent (Despark, Anguished Unmaking)
ten.why: {2}{W} instant, destroy target nonland permanent, and the 1/1 it hands the opponent is the price for covering both artifacts and both enchantments in one card — Feed the Swarm misses Torpor Orb and Vandalblast misses the two enchantments.
ten.unlocks: The answer component goes from two cards to three, and Despark's mana-value-4 floor stops being the deck's only instant-speed line against a three-mana tax enchantment.

ten.closes: engine: the four-card conversion layer (TOKEN -> DAMAGE)
ten.why: "Whenever another creature you control enters, this deals 1 damage to each opponent" is Impact Tremors on a body, and it takes the conversion layer from four cards to five — the component measured at 52.5% drawn, mean turn 3.28, and the thinnest half of the go-wide kill at 40.2%.
ten.unlocks: A fifth converter that is itself a creature, so casting it under Purphoros or Warleader's Call already deals damage, and it arrives on the same three mana as the payoffs it joins.

ten.why: Untapped, any colour, one damage — swapped for Spectator Seating it is a straight +1 black source with no white or red given back, moving the worst-colour figure from 26 against a target of 36 to 27, and it adds no tapland to a deck that keeps only three.
ten.unlocks: One more turn-one Swamp for Cordial Vampire's {B}{B} and one more line to Bloodletter of Aclazotz's {1}{B}{B}{B}, the two deepest pip demands in the deck.

ten.closes: engine: the eight-card token multiplier and extra-maker component
ten.why: Three tokens per attack in a four-player pod — six under Anointed Procession, nine under Ojer Taq — and every one of them is a creature entering, so a single attack step feeds Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Corpse Knight three to nine times over.
ten.unlocks: Width that does not need a Vampire spell to be cast, which is the one thing the eminence trigger cannot give you on a turn you hold up removal.

ten.closes: engine: the eight-card token multiplier and extra-maker component
ten.why: Triples every creature token instead of doubling it, so one eminence trigger under Anointed Procession is six bodies rather than two, and each body is another Impact Tremors trigger at all three seats.
ten.unlocks: The highest ceiling available on the trigger kill, and it comes back as a land when it dies, which is more than any other six-drop in the identity offers a board that just ate a wrath.

ten.why: Impact Tremors is a red source and so are Purphoros, Warleader's Call and Witty Roastmaster: Torbran turns each of those triggers from 1 or 2 damage into 3 or 4, which is the difference between a two-mana Vampire dealing 12 to each opponent and dealing lethal on the spot. The cost is honest — {1}{R}{R}{R} against 17 red sources is the deepest pip demand anyone would add to this deck, and four maindeck red cards already sit under their line.
ten.unlocks: A ceiling raise on the kill route the deck already verifies, rather than a fourth copy of a component that assembles 78% of the time.

gaps: The Bloodthirsty Conqueror singleton gets no pick and that is deliberate. The only true replacement for its half of the loop is a second 'whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life', and no other card in this colour identity reads that way — Marauding Blight-Priest, Epicure of Blood and Starscape Cleric are all the other half, the half Vito and Sanguine Bond already cover. Spending a slot there would buy redundancy on the wrong side.

Whether Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles damage-sourced life loss is unsettled; the checker-passed lines cover pure life loss only. That decides both the Mirkwood Bats pairing and the Torbran arithmetic, and /resolve-stack is what settles it.

Whether a doubled token-creation event triggers Mirkwood Bats once or twice is the single figure that decides whether it is a fifth converter or a second Impact Tremors. It needs a stack scenario, not an assertion.

No artifact measures cast rates, only draw rates. The double-white picks (Skyclave Apparition, Adeline) and the triple-red one (Torbran) are priced against Karsten's rows — 21 white sources against the 26 a {1}{W}{W} card asks, 17 red against a triple pip — and not against any observed failure.

Nothing measures how often a land answer matters at this table. Generous Gift and Vindicate are the only two picks that reach the class, and the case for them rests on the tax permanents they also answer, not on land destruction.

The pilot named surviving a sweeper as a want and no pick answers it. The protection component is six cards at 68.1%, four of them board-wide, and every candidate that would deepen it — Clever Concealment, Unbreakable Formation — competes with an answer suite the diagnosis calls the binding constraint. Say the word and it becomes the eleventh pick.
